mechanism_narrative: The observed consistent week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks indicates a sustained recovery trend that will continue to drive retail and recreation activity higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rebound in WORKPLACES mobility, exceeding a 5-point increase week-on-week, signals a return to office-based work which directly increases demand for retail and recreation services during weekdays, leading to higher RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days despite WORKPLACES rising by more than 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The combined increase in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility suggests a broader return to pre-pandemic commuting patterns, which will synergistically boost foot traffic in retail and recreation areas, leading to higher RETAIL_REC.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, even with concurrent increases in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicating fewer people staying home, suggests a shift towards out-of-home activities, which will directly translate to increased engagement with retail and recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC higher.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5% change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL mobility falling below 5% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The strong and consistent upward trend in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, often a leading indicator of general public movement and confidence, suggests an overall increase in out-of-home activity that will spill over into retail and recreation, leading to higher RETAIL_REC.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in PARKS mobility, falling below -15% from baseline for two consecutive weeks, indicates a shift away from outdoor leisure activities, potentially redirecting consumer spending and time towards indoor retail and recreation venues, leading to higher RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 7 days despite PARKS mobility falling below -15% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As RETAIL_REC shows a positive trend and RESIDENTIAL mobility remains stable or slightly declines, it indicates a reallocation of time from home-based activities to out-of-home consumption, reinforcing the upward trajectory of retail and recreation.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than the last 14 days, despite RETAIL_REC showing a positive trend and RESIDENTIAL remaining stable or declining.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained recovery across multiple mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, WORKPLACES, TRANSIT) without any new policy restrictions being observed implies growing public confidence in safety, which will encourage further engagement with retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, despite continued recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT and no new policy restrictions.
